Katalog Berita (Halaman 50/58)

#1687. Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: Resolute Gunners dig in for a big Anfield win

Fourteen years is a long time to wait for a win at any stadium, but Arsenal ensured all three points returned from Anfield to North London for the first time since 2012 yesterday.

The surprise in the team line-up was the return of Christos Tzolis who had missed a month, more or less, with a hamstring injury. If it initially felt a bit harsh on Eberechi Eze, Mikel Arteta’s post-game comments about him barely making the game because of an injury problem of his own made it make more sense.

Early on, we were really good. Plenty of the ball, playing it well in their half, and lots of control. Liverpool looked a bit off the pace, and in the opening minutes young midfielder Trey Nyoni was lucky to escape without some sanction for a nasty foul on Martin Odegaard. I think it was much more mistimed than malicious, but studs down the Achilles is never good, and we saw Crystal Palace striker Jean Philippe Mateta see red for something similar on Saturday evening.

The early pressure paid dividends when Liverpool were a little sloppy at the back. Odegaard pounced to recover the ball, it was fed to Noni Madueke via Bruno Guimaraes, and when Declan Rice overlapped, his precision ball to the back post found Kai Havertz for a tap-in to make it 1-0. That makes it 5 assists so far this season for the midfielder, all of them from open play as well, and his presence in this team reminds me so much of Patrick Vieira. Not that they’re the same kind of player, but that his importance and stature is just fundamental to us. The desire he showed with that overlap is, essentially, what cracked this game open in our favour.

There was another back post chance for Havertz, almost getting on the end of a deflected Guimaraes shot, but after that – as happens so often at Anfield – the momentum changed. This time there was no Granit Xhaka style confrontation to act as a catalyst, the game just shifted and in the final 20 minutes of the first half we rode our luck a bit.

Liverpool started to play around our box and deliver dangerous balls. One almost found Alexander Isak but a combination of David Raya and Ezri Konsa was enough to see it trickle wide. Florian Wirtz hit the bar with a free kick, and Liverpool wanted a penalty when Tzolis looked to pull back Cody Gakpo but I don’t think there was enough in that one. The next one, however, oooof.

Liverpool put in another dangerous cross, Isak was there to head towards goal from close range, and Jurrien Timber’s shirt pull absolutely prevented him from making contact with the ball. You know my rule of thumb with penalties: how would I feel it were given, or not given, up the other end, and if we didn’t get that I’d be fuming. It’s a penalty all day long, and even if the ref didn’t quite see the foul well enough, the VAR officials really ought to have suggested an on-field review. I found the focus on Isak’s reaction a bit odd. Surely the onus is on the officials to recognise what we’ve all seen without a player having to prompt them in that direction, but we got so, so lucky there.

As we did when Alexis Mac Allister ran into the box and, unmarked from 10 yards out, headed the ball over the bar when he absolutely should score. That was a very bad miss from a Liverpool perspective, and a huge chance to equalise just before the break. We needed half-time, and despite the fact Liverpool enjoyed plenty of the ball in the early part of the second period, they looked a lot less dangerous.

My explanation for this is that we leaned into one of our great strengths, which is our defensive organisation and discipline. I thought Konsa was outstanding, but so too was Riccardo Calafiori at left-back whose one on one defending has improved massively. He dealt with Gakpo, he then had to contend with Rio Ngumoha, and I just loved the concentration as he focused on the ball and more often than not prevented Liverpool from creating danger.

Myles Lewis-Skelly came on midfield, Odegaard’s pressing was relentless, and as I remarked on BlueSky afterwards, if this team could attack half as well as it can defend, we’d be the best team in the world by a mile. There were moments when we could have countered better and with more pace, but we still found some threat in the second 45. The best chance fell to Tzolis, set up by Madueke, and his first-time shot was heading for the bottom corner but for a brilliant save from Alisson.

Liverpool threw the kitchen sink at it from the bench, but it made little difference. Mac Allister then got a bit naughty, slapping Odegaard on the back of the head, then collapsing to the ground to make it look as if Madueke had leaned his head into him. Replays showed that didn’t happen, and it was pretty pathetic from the Argentina international. I guess, as well as being a risible piece of play-acting, there was an element of desperation to it, because Liverpool huffed and puffed but could not blow our house down because of how defensively outstanding we are as a team.

For the first time in Premier League history, Liverpool finished a home game without a shot on target, which tells you something. It probably tells you just how much that Timber shirt pull had an impact because a striker like Isak would at least have tested David Raya from there, but more broadly it tells you that this is a team who look laser-focused on their target this season which is to retain the title – something we’ve never done in the modern era.

Afterwards, I thought the manager’s turn of phrase was interesting when he referred to it as ‘a mission’, saying:

Just loving the mission and the mission was something that we didn’t accomplish in 14 years. You really need to enjoy that. If you don’t, there will be a moment that you will switch off and they will punish you. I think the way we competed and played and the chances that we generated as well, it was really impressive so I’m really happy.

He’s obviously referencing winning away at Liverpool for the first time in such a long time, but I think it applies to the season as well. And, as I referenced in yesterday’s blog, there was a response to the midweek defeat to Fleetwood Town. If that was a result that as fans we could find relatively easy to compartmentalise, I don’t think the same is true for this manager because we know he wants to win every game, and it how much it stings when we don’t – especially against lower league opposition. He expected his side to deliver, saying:

It was a feeling, how the hell can that happen? How can you get out of the cup when you shoot 27 times? We had the chances that we had against a team that had put one shot on target and then you look so silly. Then you have to go to Anfield and say, how can I lift those players up? I had a feeling and I said, now is the moment. We’re going to have to dig deep, have an element of luck at times and for sure a lot of quality in the key moments and we’ve done it.

Which I think is a pretty fair assessment. We did a lot of stuff very well, we had moments of luck – which you so often need in a game like this to take all three points – but I don’t think anyone should be under any illusions that this was anything other than the champions demonstrating our title credentials again. In every season, regardless of how good you are, you need the rub of the green from time to time, like a Ruud van Nistelrooy penalty miss at Old Trafford, or Mateus Fernandes missing a huge chance for West Ham. It doesn’t change the inherent quality you possess or what you’re capable of doing, and in the cold light of day it should make you more driven to ensure you widen the margins – and by that I mean delivering a bit more in the opposition’s final third.

However, no complaints this morning. We had a job to do, and a difficult one at that, and we did exactly that to put us back on top of the table. It’s a nice place to be, but it’s still so early in the season I think we should dismiss any chat about what it means at this point. We can be impressed, but still cognisant of the fact there’s still a long, long way to go.

Right, I’ll leave it there for now, but we will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on today. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around noon or so. Until then, have a good one.

#1685. Wesley Fofana has a shot at redemption after shocking first half in Man United win, Estevao cements his status as Chelsea's fan favourite - and why Romeo Lavia was their star man, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 02:01 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 04:27 EDT, 1 November 2026

There is something called the Science of Scare Project.

It is a study ranking the most frightening films of all time by measuring an audience’s reaction to watching them. Via their average heart rate, highest spike, time between heartbeats, and so on.

Halloween enthusiasts consulting this year’s eerie list found the spookiest ever was a 2012 supernatural horror called Sinister. That received a 'Scare Score' of 96/100. It beat The Conjuring (88/100), Paranormal Activity (73/100), Texas Chainsaw Massacre (65/100), and so on.

If only the good folks behind this scientific study had hooked up the Chelsea fans at Stamford Bridge. It would have been intriguing to know the fluctuating activity of their hearts as they watched Wesley Fofana flirt with gifting Manchester United the opening goal.

We would have seen the spikes occur whenever he was involved. Chelsea’s major mistakes came from the 25-year-old Frenchman, who will be needed more while Maxence Lacroix is recovering from his hamstring injury.

Xabi Alonso has told us Lacroix is facing ‘a few weeks’ on the sidelines, but sources around the player have suggested he may not return until 2027. That information has also been stood up by the odd contact at the club.

Chelsea’s major mistakes came from the 25-year-old Frenchman, who will be needed more

Chelsea supporters were thrilled they got to watch Estevao (left) and now he has given Alonso a selection headache

Which is worrying for Alonso and Co. While Chelsea wound up winning 2-0 against an abysmal United team now hovering over the relegation zone, Fofana’s first half was a shocker.

First, he was burgled of the ball by the halfway line. Amad countered, and while he should have made more of the chance, he won a corner. United scored from this attacking phase, but Chelsea survived when VAR decided the scorer, Matheus Cunha, was offside.

Then, Fofana misjudged a long pass to leave Amad with only Mike Penders to beat. Chelsea got away with that one, too.

This followed what happened at Anfield on Wednesday when Chelsea exited the Carabao Cup. Fofana swapped football for volleyball at a Liverpool corner to hand them their penalty equaliser. At the shootout, he was the unfortunate soul who skied the decisive spot-kick to confirm defeat.

If Alonso had any other senior central defenders available on his bench, he might have made the change at half-time versus United. He did not, and so Fofana survived a hooking.

To Fofana’s credit, he calmed after the break. He was the one clattered to win Chelsea their penalty and earn Lisandro Martinez his second yellow. There was even a point towards the end, when Chelsea were leading 2-0 against United’s 10 men, that he was trying to pass from the back.

Bruno Fernandes stood in his way and so he simply nutmegged his opponent to find Valentin Barco. As Fofana jogged by Fernandes immediately afterwards, he rubbed it in a little, laughing at United’s captain with a little finger-wagging gesture.

That told us the confidence is there, though Chelsea fans will continue to fear he is a player too prone to a clanger, rather than a centre back who cost £75million from Leicester City in 2022.

Even before his errors here, there were pieces penned by other websites suggesting he should be seen as the worst signing of the BlueCo era. Thanks to his driving infringements, we know how much he earns, too. More than £200,000 per week, his lawyer had to tell Lavender Hill Magistrates' Court in January as his client reached a remarkable 50 points on his licence.

It is fair to say he has not lived up to the hype which accompanied his arrival with injuries having hampered his career. But here is a small chance at redemption. Lacroix may miss the remainder of 2026, and Fofana will be needed. Chelsea would love him to reduce his 'Scare Score' which, in the first half of this win over United, was rivalling Sinister’s record.

Those of us inside Stamford Bridge did not notice it. We thought Bryan Mbeumo had sent his shot straight into the crossbar. But then we saw Penders celebrating, and the slow-mo replays.

Penders got his fingertips to it. He stopped any chance it had of creeping underneath the crossbar to reduce the scoreline to 2-1. The 21-year-old Belgian earned this clean sheet.

It was good to see. He had a nightmare against Tottenham, there is no hiding from that. He punched a cross into his own goal to give Spurs their opener in that 2-0 defeat. But at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, he responded well. Then here against United, he would not be beaten.

There has been talk of Chelsea rushing back Martinez from his jaw injury, maybe by having him wear a protective mask. But Penders performing like this may mean that is not necessary.

The loudest cheer when the line-ups were announced was reserved for Estevao, followed by Stamford Bridge chanting ‘Stevo, Stevo’. They love him, and they are right to love him.

He had to wait a long time for his first Premier League start of the season. Arguably too long.

But he seized his opportunity. Estevao scored two goals – alas, both were disallowed for offside – but he was forever involved. Chelsea supporters were thrilled they got to watch him, and now, he has given Alonso a selection headache because it was a showing which said he should start more.

Daily Mail Sport reported in our Chelsea Confidential column this week how there had been no fallout between Alonso and Estevao, despite speculation suggesting otherwise. His exclusion from the line-up was down to tactical and technical decisions.

When Estevao thought he had scored for the second time, he ran over to Alonso to give him a hug. When substituted, there was another cuddle. All is fine in that relationship, even if the 19-year-old Brazilian is itching to play more.

Lavia was actually the best performer in this victory. It was his winning of the ball that led to Rogers scoring

Jordan Henderson fell ill and so was unable to start his sixth successive match for Chelsea.

But that afforded an opportunity to Romeo Lavia. He had completed his first full 90 in a competitive game for Chelsea at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup. Then, a day before this Premier League visit of United, he was told he would need to start again.

Despite TNT Sports being blinded by Morgan Rogers’ fine opener – they gave him the player-of-the-match award – Lavia was actually the best performer in this victory. It was his winning of the ball that led to Rogers scoring. He then completed yet another full 90. You wait for one bus, then two come along at once.

#1684. Arsenal transfer news: Martin Zubimendi ready to leave this winter, seven European giants informed

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 10:31, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 10:31

Short of game time at Arsenal, Martin Zubimendi is ready to leave the London club in the January transfer window. Seven European clubs have been informed.

In the summer of 2025, Arsenal beat several clubs, notably Real Madrid, to sign Martin Zubimendi. Arsenal spent £59.5m (€70m) to sign the Spain midfielder from Real Sociedad. After an encouraging first season, the 27-year-old is having a difficult start to the campaign.

He has made 10 appearances and has started only twice, both in the EFL Cup. Martin Zubimendi has played just 15 minutes in the Champions League and 99 in the Premier League. He has become a rotation player in Mikel Arteta’s mind. This situation is hard for the Spain international to accept.

According to TeamTalk, Zubimendi is ready to leave Arsenal in January to try to relaunch his career. He wants more playing time. Many major European clubs are aware of this decision taken by the midfielder.

Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid have all shown an interest in a return to La Liga for the former Real Sociedad man. Real Madrid have been long-term admirers of the San Sebastian native.

It remains to be seen whether this opportunity will change the plans of Real Madrid, who had decided not to sign anyone this winter.

In Germany, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund have been informed of the possibility of signing Martin Zubimendi this winter. The same goes for Chelsea and Liverpool in England. It remains to be seen whether one of these European giants will now be ready to make a move this winter.

In this affair, Arsenal are aware of their player’s desire to leave the club this winter and are preparing to open the door for him.

A loan departure is a possible option. It would notably allow Arsenal, who invested £59.5m (€70m) a little over a year ago, to hope that Zubimendi relaunches himself in the second half of the season so as to secure a higher transfer fee next summer.

#1682. Fridges and pigs and scoring goals

We live in strange times. Sorry to start your day with this shocking revelation, I realise this is a bit of a bolt from the blue, but it’s fact. All across Europe supermarket fridges are being hacked. What a time to be alive. They used to hack, I dunno, mainframes and banks and shit, but now they’re hacking fridges.

Maybe they just got bored taking billions of made-up money from CryptoSloth and BitWomble and needed a challenge. I feel like fridges ought to be the kind of thing you just can’t hack – beyond unplugging it – but what do I know? Anyway, it’s an example of how the inter-connectivity that brings us all together every day is being weaponised and now the sliced meats in your local store are gone off because Neo pwned some large cold cupboards. As if we don’t have enough to deal with.

Such as all the people who hate the way Arsenal play. Let me be very clear, my days of caring what other people think about this football club, or pretty much anything else that’s important to me, are gone. It’s a waste of time. It’s a bit like quote that’s often attributed to George Bernard Shaw, which says ‘Never wrestle with pigs. You both get dirty and the pig likes it.’

I don’t think he actually said that, but I think we can all connect with the meaning. It applies so much to social media, and to many of the ways we’re exposed to punditry and ‘expert’ analysis in football these days. Like one of those shows where you have a couple of ex-pro pigs bleating on about this and that, and then a collection of other little pigs who support all the clubs argue with them and amongst themselves, and it’s just a pigstravaganza of pointless, inane bollocks but it does #numbers on socials so is seen as valuable #content.

I understand why opposition fans go on and on about how much they hate how Arsenal play. It’s because we win a lot of games. That’s the thing that really irks them. That’s just so basic though, you can’t appear to be clever and an aficionado of the game if you just say ‘I don’t like it when they win’, so it’s dressed up as dismissal of style or something else.

And look, here’s where the strange world we live in comes back into focus. You can, and really should, be able to hold more than one thought in your brain – about football or anything else – that holds true. I absolutely love how good we are defensively. LOVE IT. The commitment with which we are determined not to give the opposition anything is truly something to relish. Players laser-focused on their one on ones; putting bodies on the line to block shots and crosses; 11 players moving like a murmuration of birds because they’re so well drilled and organised; off the awareness and discipline; brilliantly timed tackles and headers and clearances; lads sticking up for each other when the opposition get a bit snide, as we saw on Sunday with Jurrien Timber and Noni Madueke refusing to allow their captain to be treated that way; it’s all part of a brilliantly defiant defensive attitude that runs right through this team.

Creating that is not easy. As Arsenal fans we have endured defences that were porous and feeble and, at times, very, very stupid. I do not long for a return to those times. Over the years Mikel Arteta has assembled a collection of players who cannot wait to go out there and do the dirty work of defending, and it runs from front to back because that’s what he demands. If it was that easy, everyone would do it, so to castigate a team’s brilliance in one department because you just lost to them without a shot on target just comes across as sour grapes.

Here’s the other thought though. I’d really like us to be a bit better from an attacking perspective, and when I look at this team and what it’s capable of, there’s no question the forward line remains the area where you can see the room for improvement. We defend as well as we do because, more often than you or I might like, we have to – because we live through games of fine margins. A 1-0 to the Arsenal is part of our history, hard-wired into our supporter DNA (particularly if you’re of a particular vintage), but I can’t lie and wish there weren’t a few more 3-0s to the Arsenal.

I’m absolutely certain Mikel Arteta would like that too, and I think it’s a bit too easy to say that this is a team that plays precisely the football he wants it to play. He is, as we all understand, an arch pragmatist, so what we get is a team that leans into its strengths, as laid out above. He is characterised as a defensive coach, which I get, but a few seasons ago we found an attacking cocktail that drove a title challenge, and saw us score more goals that year than the Invincibles did when they won the league in 2004 (91 to 73).

I think he wants both. He wants that parsimony at the back and the firepower up front. Unfortunately, forward line recruitment is the most difficult part of transfer business, and while he as manager has a part to play in that, as a club our track record is quite poor in that regard. This summer’s window was a complete bust from an attacking perspective, not a good look when you’re pursuing players like Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez. When you then let three forwards go and add just one, there are questions to be asked of the people in charge. Arteta among them, of course, but he’s not the one whose job it is to get the deals done.

It’s why there are so many conversations around January, and what we might do. We see other clubs recruit forwards who produce on a consistent basis, while ours too often struggle to find that end product. Is it our system? Would these players find it hard to get those goals for us? Reasonable questions, but the bottom line in my opinion is that we have A+ options at the back and in midfield, while in that front three we’re a bit C-. That’s where the room for improvement is, that’s where the recruitment needs to be better (certainly better than no recruitment at all), and that’s how the games we currently win by a single goal margin, often by virtue of our defensive strength, become a bit more routine.

Simplistic? Yes. Easier said than done? Quite probably. But necessary? Absolutely. Until then though, expect more defensive masterclasses, more pig wrestling, and perhaps someone could hack our own Swedish fridge into scoring a few more goals. Worth a try!

Right, I’ll leave it there for now. I just have a small favour to ask. Arseblog has been nominated for Best Fan Media (Fran Merida) in the 2026 FSA Awards. We’re trying to retain our title, so if you could take a moment to give us a vote that would be much appreciated. You can do that here – https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/fsa-awards-2026

#1680. Cardinale: “Milan were at the top of the world, and we’re going to bring them back there”

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale spoke to CBS Sports before the derby win over Inter, pledging to bring the club back to the summit of football.

On Halloween night, the Rossoneri ensured that Inter’s derby nightmare continued as Milan won their fourth consecutive victory in the fixture, extending the unbeaten run against the Nerazzurri to eight meetings in the process.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

All of the damage was done in the first half. Christian Pulisic struck in the fourth minute with a header, Adrien Rabiot scored from a corner six minutes later, Alessandro Bastoni halved the deficit and then Diego Moreira converted a lovely free-kick to reopen the two-goal advantage.

In the end, 3-1 is how it would stay, securing a memorable win. Cardinale spoke with the CBS panel in the build-up to kick-off at San Siro last night and he shed a bit more light on his plans for the Rossoneri moving forward. His words are via MilanNews.

“Well, first of all, this stadium… As an American, I can say that a stadium like this is something you never see anywhere else. Tonight, it’s going to light up. There’s something different about this derby tonight than in the past.

“There’s an electricity here that I’ve never felt before. You’ll see nearly 80,000 people literally shaking this structure. It’s going to be truly incredible.”

“It is. You know, when we bought the club four years ago, I started working on this right away. And part of what we’re trying to do here is bring the best of America to Italian soccer, and specifically to AC Milan.

“It’s extraordinary: most people didn’t think we could accomplish all this, or even get to this point. Not only did we announce the stadium this week, but we also announced the largest naming rights deal in history. I think it’s a wonderful thing for Italian soccer.

“The message to everyone is that we’re coming back. Italian soccer truly deserves to be at the top again, and we’ll do everything we can through AC Milan to make that happen.”

“There’s a connection between us. We’re two guys from Pennsylvania trying to make their way and understand Italy. He’s ‘Captain America’, but he’s also my franchise player. I couldn’t be more thrilled to have him with us.

“It’s a true partnership with him. He’s a leader, and his presence on the court makes all the difference in the world. You’ve seen it this year: when he steps on the court, he completely changes the game.”

Why is AC Milan and winning with Milan so important to you?

“I remember George Steinbrenner telling me about twenty years ago, ‘Don’t get too emotionally involved in all this; don’t go into the locker room, don’t do those things’. But in this case, I got emotionally involved.

“For me, it became a personal issue. And I don’t know what it is: maybe it’s just that… look around, listen. This means so much to the people of Milan, it has a huge impact on them, and I feel a huge responsibility.

“AC Milan were at the top of the world, and we’re going to bring them back there. This will probably be one of the greatest things I’ll do in my career.”

“It’s something multigenerational. This stadium is an icon. Look around, look at these people: this means everything to them. All of this carries with it an enormous amount of responsibility, it almost makes your wrists tremble.

“The best thing I can do is do my job well to help this club win, because victory spreads to the whole community. Listen… can you hear? That’s the Curva. You don’t see anything like it in America, it’s truly special.”

What’s your favourite detail of the new stadium?

“What we tried to do with the new stadium was to live up to the name and tradition of this facility. This is San Siro, but it is also ‘La Scala del Calcio’, the opera house of football.

“When you look at the design of the new stadium, those majestic, slender lines on the exterior recall the grand drapes and curtains of La Scala. It is our tribute to the history of this city.”

How did you manage to unblock the stadium situation?

“It’s been an incredible collaboration, a true partnership with our president Paolo Scaroni and the mayor. It’s extraordinary because everyone told me it’s impossible to build a stadium here in Italy. The last major stadium built in Italy was in 2011 in Turin, with about 40,000 seats.

“The extraordinary thing about our project is that it will be a 75,000-seat stadium, and we expect to have it completed before the 2032 European Championships. It will be a great thing for all of Italy.”

#1679. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

The final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

How on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

Those two goals late in the half completely change the complexion of the game and Michael Carrick’s half-time team talk. Good first 45 minutes back in the Champions League for United.

The first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

Sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:

Sabah FC have named a starting XI featuring 11 different nationalities 🌍🇰🇿 Stas Pokatilov🇩🇿 Akim Zedadka🇦🇿 Rahman Dashdamirov🇿🇦 Aden McCarthy🇵🇱 Tymoteusz Puchacz🇺🇿 Umarali Rakhmonaliev🇭🇷 Ivan Lepinjica🇯🇲 Kaheem Parris🇷🇸 Veljko Simic🇳🇬 Christian Nwachukwu🇷🇼 Joy-Lance… pic.twitter.com/ih5Sf1aeie

Mazraoui, despite starting at right-back, has already had three shots in the game. Two have been outside the box that have been blocked and the latest hits the side netting from the right side of the penalty area.

Mazraoui plays a pass forward into Cunha on the right side of the box and the Brazilian tries to beat Pokatilov at the near post but the Sabah keeper makes the save and pushes it around the post for a corner.

Sabah are able to clear their lines from Mbeumo’s delivery.

Sabah seem content to take risks on the ball deep inside their own half and play out from the back. Will that be a masterstroke or is it asking for trouble?

Sabah make their first foray into the Manchester United penalty area and there are appeals for handball. It did hit Dorgu’s hand but it was right down by his side and that is not a deliberate handball. Sabah do win a corner, which Dorgu heads away.

Sesko, fresh off what he thought was going to be the winner at Everton on Sunday, has been given the nod to start up top for the home side tonight. He is very close to closing the Sabah goalkeeper Pokatilov down inside his own six-yard box and that was nearly a horrific moment for the Champions League debutants a matter of minutes into their debut in this competition.

Sabah started their journey through the qualifying rounds of this comeptition back in the early parts of July so they have already played quite a number of games so far this season, in comparison to Manchester United’s three competitive fixtures coming into tonight.

As has been the case at every Champions League game this week, there is a moment silence to remember the victims of the recent deadly floods in Nepal.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Manchester United, three-time winners of this trophy, return to the Champions League whilst Sabah make their debut in the competition.

It’s 1,003 days since the Champions League anthem has been heard at Old Trafford and, to be honest, it feels longer. There are about 500 Sabah fans here tonight.

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Sabah: Pokatilov, McCarthy, Dashdamirov, Rakhmonaliev, Nwachukwu, Parris, Lepinjica, Mickels, Simic, Puchacz, Zedadka.Substitutes: Ramazanov, Mirzammadov, Khaibulaev, Isaev, Rustamli, Mutallimov, Almeida, Quiroz, Fernandes, Mukhtarov, Mbina.

As we speak, there have just been two goals scored in the last few moments in the two early kick-offs. Both home sides, Fenerbahce and PSV, have just equalised in their respective games.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#1678. Harry Kane embraces his family during special Ballon d'Or presentation at Bayern Munich - before England skipper MISSES a penalty in chaotic draw!

Published: 06:28 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:29 EDT, 1 November 2026

Harry Kane received a hero's welcome as he returned to action for Bayern Munich for the first time since winning the Ballon d'Or.

Kane was crowned as the best player in the world on Monday night, becoming the first English player to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001 on what was an emotional evening for the former Tottenham star.

His success came off the back of a stunning year with Bayern and England, with the forward netting a staggering 73 goals during the 2025-26 season.

Kane's goals spearheaded the German side's domestic Treble, while he also captained his country to third place at the World Cup.

And, ahead of Bayern's clash against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday night, Kane received a special presentation at the Allianz Arena.

With both sets of players and match officials lined up on the pitch, Kane was welcomed out of the tunnel while holding his new prized possession in his hands.

Harry Kane presented his Ballon d'Or trophy to Bayern Munich fans and players on Saturday

Kane received a hero's welcome from Bayern fans and his team-mates as he walked out

Kane was also greeted by his family, including his four children, ahead of the match

Bayern's players and fans gave Kane a standing ovation as Land of Hope and Glory played over the stadium's sound system.

The England skipper was serenaded by the home faithful, although some Dortmund fans could be heard to be booing him.

Waiting on the pitch were his family, including his wife Kate, four children, his parents and his brother Charlie, and he greeted them all as he came out.

Kane then took a microphone and addressed the home fans by saying: 'I’m extremely proud to be a Bayern player.

'The support you’ve shown me since I arrived is incredible. I’m extremely proud to present this to you. I hope to win many more titles with you.'

Unfortunately for Kane, his on-pitch return didn't perhaps go as planned as he missed a penalty as Bayern drew 2-2 with Dortmund.

Kane had the chance to mark his honour further after Konrad Laimer had put Bayern ahead, but he smacked his spot kick against the bar.

Serhou Guirassy then equalised for Dortmund, and although Kane assisted Dayot Upemecano's response, which put his side 2-1 up, former Wolves flop Fabio Silva equalised for the visitors in the 89th minute.

Kane addressed the crowd on the pitch where he highlighted his pride at playing for Bayern

Meanwhile, after winning the award on Monday, Kane had made sure to pay tribute to Bayern.

He said: 'Without you guys [Bayern Munich team-mates] and the rest of the team it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete, so thank you very much.

'To Vinny [Vincent Kompany]. I know he is at home or still in the hospital. Wishing you well. I hope this gave you a bit of energy. To all the staff, the we way train and the way you push us, it is a credit to yourself.

'Since I have been with you I have improved as a player, improved as a person and a leader.

'It is an honour to play for Bayern Munich, to represent you is a real privilege and I am glad to be bringing this trophy back to Bayern Munich.'

Manchester United and Bayern Munich are reportedly both interested in signing FC Twente’s Ruud Nijstad during next summer's transfer window.

Nijstad, 18, is believed to be on the radar of a number of major clubs, with Twente facing a battle to keep hold of him on a long-term basis given his development.

According to Twente Insite, both Man United and Bayern are keen to secure his signature next year, while a number of other European teams are in the race.

Twente are in a strong position when it comes to the defender's future given that he signed a new contract in July until the summer of 2029.

Nijstad featured on 24 occasions for Twente last season and has played 17 times in all competitions during the 2026-27 campaign.

In total, the centre-back has played 41 times for his current team, scoring twice and registering one assist, while he has been capped twice by Netherlands Under-19s.

Former Man United manager Erik ten Hag has been Twente's technical director since February, and the Dutchman recently commented on the teenager's future.

“I don’t know, but there is indeed interest in him. Several clubs from the top eight in Europe have made concrete offers. But he simply made a very conscious choice to play for FC Twente this season,” said Ten Hag.

“He is a very great talent who joined the team last season. He is still very young, but he does so in a very self-assured manner. It is a pleasure to work with that boy. Quite a few clubs from the top of Europe have come forward. I think that is only a good thing.

“It is also particularly nice that he very consciously chose to stay with Twente for at least another year. Maybe even longer, but in any case, this season.”

Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire could both leave next summer, meanwhile, with two new centre-backs therefore potentially being targeted.

Leny Yoro is regarded as a key part of the Man United defence moving forwards, but there is also uncertainty surrounding the futures of both Ayden Heaven and Matthijs de Ligt.

By Matt Law | 03 Nov 2026 12:08, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 12:10

Manchester United have reportedly been 'alerted' to the possibility that Lennart Karl could leave Bayern Munich during next summer's transfer window.

The 18-year-old has represented Bayern's first team on 52 occasions, scoring 10 goals and registering 10 assists in the process.

The four-time Germany international has a contract at Allianz Arena until the summer of 2029, but there is currently a host of speculation surrounding his future.

Recent comments from Bayern's honorary president Uli Hoeness on Karl are not believed to have been well-received by the youngster's reprensentatives.

"He is far from being a superstar," Hoeness told Welt am Sonntag. "Young players need humility. I don’t know whether it is good for Lennart Karl to always be over-protected. The comparisons with [Michael] Olise do not help him at all. There is still a massive difference between them."

According to Bild, the comments have caused 'unrest' in the Karl camp, which has alerted Man United to a possible transfer next summer.

The report claims that Liverpool and Arsenal are also keeping a close eye on the situation, with the teenager potentially available for £50m next summer.

Earlier this year, Karl called Real Madrid his "dream club".

“Bayern is a very very big club. It's a dream to play there. But at some point I definitely want to go to Real Madrid. That's my dream club. Of course, Bayern is something very special and it's a lot of fun at the club," Karl told Sky Deutschland.

Karl's comments did not go down well with Bayern, and it is believed that there is friction behind the scenes, which could ultimately lead to a departure.

The teenager has scored once and registered two assists in 12 appearances for Bayern at the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

Karl largely operates as a number 10, but he can also feature off the right, and the German could potentially be a long-term replacement for Bruno Fernandes at Old Trafford.

Fernandes has struggled this season, and the 32-year-old's contract is due to expire at the end of the campaign, albeit with the option to extend for a further year.

#1674. Opinion: Liverpool have already found their perfect successor for 85-goal sensation

Liverpool's performances this season have been a tad ropey.

They're fifth in the Premier League with their most recent game ending in a 1-0 defeat to Arsenal.

And, while Liverpool weren't the favourites going into that game, they still should have done better than they did.

If they'd have performed even half as well as they can, things would have been massively different.

Obviously, that wasn't how things were supposed to end up and, with the January transfer window now just around the corner, many changes are expected to take place.

Liverpool may want to sign Morgan Gibbs-White as their Florian Wirtz replacement

Recently, a lot of questions have been asked about what the future has in store for Florian Wirtz at Liverpool.

Before Alexander Isak was signed on deadline day last season, the German was the Reds' most expensive signing ever.

Most people expected the former Bayer Leverkusen man to fill the creative void left by Trent Alexander-Arnold's departure and, while he did chip in with 10 assists for his teammates, everyone expected a lot more from the 23-year-old.

This season, things don't seem to have changed all that much and, even though Wirtz is being used in his preferred position of number 10, he's still failing to meet expectations.

Because of this, rumours have started to emerge with Liverpool even being linked with a move for Morgan Gibbs-White ahead of the January transfer window.

"Morgan Gibbs-White is considered one of the most attainable attacking midfield options for Manchester United," Ekrem Konur wrote.

"Interest in the Nottingham Forest star remains strong, with Tottenham and Liverpool also keeping a close eye on his situation.

"Within Manchester United's transfer plans, Gibbs-White is viewed as a more realistic target compared to several alternative options."

Morgan Gibbs-White would be a perfect transfer for Liverpool

Every single area of their squad has a player or two that could do with upgrading but, with how much money they've already spent on players, a priority list needs to be made.

Whether Liverpool believe that midfield or defence is their biggest problem, change has to occur.

Their lack of homegrown players in addition to their poor performances have led to them staying at the same level they were last term despite spending over £150 million on new players in the summer.

Of all the recent links that have emerged about Liverpool. Gibbs-White makes a lot of sense.

Not only is his best position as a number 10 but, he's also homegrown so that helps solve another issue that the Reds have.

Wirtz may have bagged 85 goals across the entirety of his career but, with the form that Gibbs-White is in this term, Liverpool adding him to their ranks would be a huge deal and would help improve their squad massively.

#1673. A chip off the old block? Wayne Rooney's son Kai, 16, is dazzling in Man United's academy after scoring FOUR goals in a game - insiders reveal the secrets behind his rise

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 07:00 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 07:06 EDT, 1 November 2026

Just over 24 years ago, a 16-year-old footballing phenomenon called Wayne Rooney made his mark with that goal for Everton against Arsenal.

Fast-forward to now and his eldest son, Kai, enhanced his burgeoning reputation while in action for Manchester United's Under 18s on Tuesday.

The 16-year-old, who turns 17 on Monday, scored four goals for the young Red Devils in a 6-0 thrashing of Burnley's U18s in the Under-18 Premier League North.

His four goals showed his repertoire of skills as the forward scored two with his preferred left foot, one with his head and the other a fine run that was finished with his right foot.

His four goals came in 44 minutes across half-time - with the latter three coming in a devastating 15-minute second-half spell (49, 63 and 66 minutes).

As Manchester United's own match report on their website details the teenager 'was the star of a clinical showing after the break from Darren Fletcher's side'.

Kai Rooney opens the scoring at Burnley for our #MUAcademy U18s 💪Watch live coverage on MUTV ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/KFr8B2hWNY

Kai Rooney scored four goals for Manchester United U18s as they thrashed Burnley U18s 6-0

One of his goals came was a penalty during Tuesday's Under-18 Premier League North fixture

Rooney's father Wayne scored that goal against Arsenal as a 16-year-old for Everton in 2002

Rooney then followed that performance with another goal in Saturday's comeback 4-1 win at Blackburn Rovers U18s, although he was later sent off for two bookable offences.

Just like his dad Wayne, Kai is fixated on football and is following in his father's footsteps in a number of ways.

As detailed by Daily Mail Sport in January, one of those is with regards to diet.

Akin to his famous father - who is United's all-time record goalscorer - in his Old Trafford heyday, Rooney Jr eats plenty of carbohydrates two days before a game. This then changes to salmon and rice followed by rice pudding the night before matches.

His dietary discipline has been recognised by those within the United academy - who are impressed by Rooney's focus.

The teenager does allow himself some respite at times though with the family's go-to is Chinese takeaway 'WowYauChow' in Altrincham. As revealed in Manchester United Confidential, crispy chilli beef is a particular favourite of the rising footballer.

Cooking has also become a passion for Rooney off-the-pitch and he is also fluent in Spanish - a trait that will only stand him in good stead in the multicultural world of football.

Rooney has had to deal with accusations of nepotism, due to the legendary figure of who his dad is, but he has always wanted to form his own path - even from a younger age than he is now.

'Kai told Wayne to stop coming to football games when he played grassroots tournaments and stuff, because he used to get swarmed, and he couldn't even watch the game,' his mum Coleen explained during her time in the I'm A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! jungle almost two years ago.

Kai is pictured with parents Coleen and Wayne signing his Man United contract when younger

Rooney is fixated with football like his father but wants to forge his own career within the sport

'How do you say to all of these kids, "Go away, I'm watching my son?" Adults, it's different, you could speak to them, so he [Kai] just said, "Oh, dad, there's no point you coming because you don't even watch me play anyway". Which is sad, but it can't be helped.'

Speaking in August 2024, Rooney underlined that he is intent on doing things his own way.

'I'm trying to make a name for myself, not try and be my dad because I'm my own person,' Kai said back in August 2024.

'I want to see how my career goes, obviously try to do the best I can and try to reach the biggest stages.

'I'm just focusing on me and to try to not let any pressure get to me and just keep working on me day by day, month by month.'

Rooney Jr has copied his father's diet when he was a professional - which includes salmon

His parents, meanwhile, have been keen to stress that they are keeping the pressure off their young son.

'He has great coaches at Manchester United, so I take a stand-off approach,' Wayne told the BBC last year.

'I speak to him, but for me it’s all about his mentality and his mindset, to make sure he keeps enjoying it – that’s the main thing for me.'

Meanwhile Coleen told The Times earlier this year: 'He’s lived it (being Wayne's son) from a young age. When we used to go to matches when he was younger, he’d get a lot of people coming up saying, "Oh, are you Wayne Rooney’s son?"

'But he’s strong-minded, always has been. I’ve got no worries in the way he deals with it.'

A Puma ambassador since he was 12, Kai used to play football in laceless boots after previously breaking both of his feet.

The youngster was signed up by Puma at the age of 12 - and has pursued a football career

Against Burnley his boots had laces as he tied his opponents in knots, something he will look to continue to do as he makes his own way in the game.

And while replicating his father seems fanciful, the iconic 'remember the name' piece of commentary could be updated for Kai in the future.

#1671. Sturm Graz vs Celje - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 03 Nov 2026 12:11

Sturm Graz play host to Celje in their fourth match of the league phase of the Europa League on Thursday night.

With these two teams having just one win between them so far, it could prove to be a pivotal fixture with regards to the final table in January.

Having missed out to Fenerbahce in Champions League qualification, Sturm Graz were presented with a brutal start to their Europa League campaign.

However, collecting four points from games against Rennes, Bournemouth and Marseille represents an excellent return as they bid to earn a spot in the top 24.

The 1-0 success over Marseille on matchday three has left Fabio Ingolitsch's side in 19th position in the league phase table.

Nevertheless, they have since posted successive draws in the Austrian Bundesliga to sit 11 points adrift of leaders Rapid Vienna.

With just five wins from 11 league contests, Ingolitsch will recognise that he needs a strong return on the continent to ensure that he keeps his job.

Meanwhile, opponents Celje find themselves down in fifth place in the Slovenian top flight.

That is despite a five-match unbeaten streak being put together across all competitions since October 18.

Included in that run is a 2-2 draw against Sturm Graz's domestic rivals Red Bull Salzburg, highlighting that Zoran Zeljkovic's side have the quality required to push their next opponents.

Since his appointment as head coach in September, he has only overseen defeats to Bayer Leverkusen, a day after his arrival, and Omonia.

Oumar Diakite came off the substitutes' bench to score Sturm Graz's equaliser at Wolfsberger AC last time out, and he could replace Belmin Beganovic down the centre of the attack.

Luis Balbo is also an option to come into the team at left wing-back, while Albert Vallci may be recalled in the back three.

Barring any fitness issues, Zeljkovic could name the same Celje XI from the 4-0 win over NK Nafta, who are in sixth place, on Sunday.

Mario Kvesic and Armandas Kucys both scored doubles in that contest, the latter finally ending his 10-game wait for a goal in this season's Slovenian top flight.

Attacking midfielder Svit Seslar is Celje's leading marksman with seven goals.

Although Sturm Graz have only scored one goal from three matches in this competition, we cannot ignore that their opponents have conceded seven. With that in mind, the Austrian giants get our backing to come through with a comfortable victory.

By Matt Law | 03 Nov 2026 12:30, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 12:32

Alejandro Balde has reportedly 'accepted' that he needs to leave Barcelona during the January transfer window for the sake of his career.

An incredibly frustrating campaign has seen the Spain international feature for just 116 minutes in all competitions, and he did not start Barcelona's league game against Alaves on Saturday even though Xavi Espart, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Eric Garcia were all out.

Balde is down the pecking order when it comes to the left-back spot at Barcelona under Hansi Flick, and according to Mundo Deportivo, the 23-year-old has 'accepted' that he will need to leave in the winter window due to his current struggles.

The report claims that the full-back is 'attracted' to the idea of playing in the Premier League amid interest from Manchester United.

The 20-time English champions were heavily linked with Balde over the summer, but the defender made it clear that he was not interested in a departure.

The situation has now changed, and it is understood that Man United are preparing to reignite their interest in January given their struggles at left-back.

Patrick Dorgu has recently returned to action, but his best football in a Man United shirt has come as an advanced option down the left.

Luke Shaw is currently injured, while neither Diogo Dalot nor Noussair Mazraoui have been convincing for Man United on the left side of the defence.

Balde has made 172 appearances for Barcelona in all competitions since breaking into their first team in 2021, scoring three goals and registering 21 assists.

The Spaniard has played 31 times in the Champions League during his career, and not too long ago, was regarded as one of the best left-backs in world football.

Barcelona boss Flick has suggested that Balde is still in his plans moving forward, with the German determined to "help" the left-back.

“What’s happening to him is normal; when you don’t play often, you lack confidence. I see him training well, but we have to decide what’s best for the team, and Joao Cancelo is in great form,” Flick told reporters during his press conference ahead of Tuesday's game with Aston Villa.

“When I say he lacks confidence, I know it can affect him, and I spoke to him after the last press conference. I respect him a lot; he’s young, but he’s a great person and a very hard worker. I’ll help him regain his confidence.”

However, most of the signs are pointing towards a January departure, and Man United now seemingly have the perfect chance to bring Balde to Old Trafford.
